subject: Materials Science
title: Galvanizing: Zinc's Double Defense
description: A fast breakdown of Galvanizing: Zinc's Double Defense for builders.

hook.text: Dip steel in molten zinc and it gains two shields — a barrier coat and a sacrificial anode in one step.

buildup.text: Hot-dip galvanizing coats steel with a thick zinc layer that forms a metallurgical bond to the surface.

discovery.text: If scratched, zinc corrodes preferentially — protecting exposed steel cathodically just like a sacrificial anode.

twist.text: Zinc forms white rust (zinc carbonate) that self-seals — a secondary protective barrier.

climax.text: Highway guardrails, transmission towers, and chain-link fences are all galvanized — lasting decades outdoors.

punchline.text: One dip in zinc gives steel a coat that fights corrosion even when damaged.

quiz.question: Why does galvanizing protect steel even when scratched?
options: Zinc acts as a sacrificial anode, corroding to protect exposed steel
Steel becomes harder at the scratch
